population.note: FICTIONAL. Series follows the Gallup 'currently taking for weight loss' measure; incretin use coded purely to type 2 diabetes is roughly stable and sits mostly outside it. Arithmetic (≈265M US adults): ever-used 15% ≈ 39.8M; current 5.9% ≈ 15.6M; used but off now 9.1% ≈ 24.2M. Of ever-users, ~80% (31.8M) have stopped at least once and ~37% of those (11.8M ≈ 30% of ever-users) have restarted at least once, consistent with the 2026 figures of roughly a third persisting at a year and 36–47% of stoppers restarting. Current 15.6M = ~8.0M who have never stopped + ~7.6M restarters now on; off-now 24.2M = 31.8M stoppers − 7.6M back on; ~4.2M restarters have stopped a second time. First-time starts fell to roughly 0.4 pp of adults over 2027–28, inside the survey margin, so ever-used still reads 15%. Almost all of the drop is people stopping who were not replaced: weight-loss coverage lost, the NAION class warning (Sep 2027), regain fatigue and the backlash. The weighted age bands (≈20/33/24/23% of adults) work out to 5.9%. Income thirds average 5.9. The bottom third is held up by Medicaid and the free HRSA programme, the top third by cash pay. Pediatric: ~0.3% of under-18s (~220k), most of them 12–17. Use at ages 6–11 rose after the Oct 2027 approval and is now skewed toward Medicaid (EPSDT obliges coverage) and the top income band, with the commercially insured middle least likely to get it.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the GLP-1 Bridge pilot ended Dec 2027 and was succeeded (Jan 2028) by a CMMI Medicare Obesity Treatment Model on the same terms (Medicare pays ~$245/month, ~$50 copay) with narrower criteria: BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with established CVD or prediabetes. Medicaid: ~22 states cover obesity at the $245 rate. EPSDT requires coverage for children 6–17 where medically necessary. New: HRSA Community Metabolic Access Program (CMAP, Jan 2028), free oral orforglipron (Foundayo) through community health centres for uninsured or underinsured adults 18–64 under 200% FPL with BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with prediabetes. Capped at 1.0M slots, sole-sourced from Lilly at a contract price of $100/month. Funded from Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff receipts.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Generic semaglutide is in ~160 countries. India has 60+ brands at ~$8–40/month, China multiple domestic generics, Canada ~CAD 70–110/month, plus Brazil, Mexico and Turkey. Cost-plus injectable generics run ~$30–140 per person-year. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Typical brand self-pay through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels is $199–299/month: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide maintenance doses at ~$199–249, retatrutide at $299 flat, oral starting doses still $149. List prices are unchanged (Wegovy $1,349) and almost nobody pays them. Employer coverage for weight management fell 60%→41% (2026→2028). Coverage is concentrated on diabetes and cardiac codes. Payer mix of the ~15.6M current weight-loss users: commercial ~5.5M (mostly under diabetes or CVD codes), cash ~4.6M, Medicare model ~2.1M, Medicaid ~1.3M, CMAP ~0.9M, gray/imported ~1.2M (≈7.7%), total 15.6M. Public spend: Medicare 2.1M × $245 × 12 ≈ $6.2B/yr; Medicaid 1.3M × $245 × 12 ≈ $3.8B/yr (federal + state); CMAP 0.9M × $100 × 12 ≈ $1.1B/yr, within its $1.2B annual allocation (1.0M × $100 × 12). The final 503B exclusion (Nov 2026) all but ended US compounding. The remaining gray market is personal import of Canadian and Indian generics by mail or across the border, tolerated in practice at personal-use volumes. China's export licensing on peptide intermediates (2027) cut the domestic compounding supply further.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, Lilly; approved Mar 2028)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema; approved Dec 2026, modest uptake)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction in obesity (tirzepatide, 2027)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction: phase 3 AUD trials of oral semaglutide under way, not approved. Some employee assistance programmes and addiction clinics prescribe off-label
pediatric use under 6 under specialist care, rare
microdosing and 'metabolic health' use by people without obesity, shrinking with the NAION warning and the end of compounding
dose-holiday cycling: users skip doses before holidays, weddings or performances to get appetite and 'edge' back
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Lilly filed the retatrutide BLA in Feb 2027 and FDA approved it in Mar 2028, 13 months later and within the ≥12-month rule. 28.3% mean loss at 80 weeks, up to ~30% at 104 weeks in BMI ≥35. Labelled for dysesthesia. ~250k patients by end-2028, held back by $299 cash pricing and thin coverage. This realises the triple-agonist driver. Amycretin is in phase 3 with readouts due 2029. Survodutide phase 3 filing expected 2029. MariTide (monthly) and bimagrumab-type muscle-preserving adjuncts are not on the US market. Phase 3 trials of oral semaglutide in alcohol use disorder are enrolling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common class effect. Concentrated at initiation and dose escalation, so it recurs with every restart, which matters more now that the population is cycling. Leading cause of discontinuation. Higher with retatrutide at top doses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis' retained.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss. Watched closely with retatrutide's larger, faster losses.
Longer RCT follow-up still finds no causal link; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL litigation continues, no verdicts against manufacturers by end-2028.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~25–40% of weight lost is lean mass. Concern sharpened by retatrutide, where roughly 30% loss puts lean-mass losses near bariatric-surgery territory. Bone-density signal under study in older adults.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Medicare model recommends resistance-training counselling; no label change. Muscle-preserving adjuncts not yet approved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. A 2027 FDA Sentinel analysis (~2.4M users) and a pooled RCT safety analysis found roughly a doubling of relative risk. Absolute risk stays low, on the order of 1–2 extra cases per 10,000 person-years, higher in people with diabetes and small optic discs.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class-wide Warnings and Precautions label (Sep 2027) covering all GLP-1-pathway agonists, including tirzepatide, retatrutide and orals. Patient Medication Guide revised. Professional societies recommend an eye history at baseline and prompt evaluation of sudden vision loss. EMA upgraded from 'very rare' in parallel.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in EMA, MHRA and later reviews.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed from labels (requested Jan 2026); remains removed.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. A 2027 prospective cohort (n≈12,000) found ~7% of users with a clinically meaningful rise in anhedonia scores vs ~3% of matched non-users. Dose-dependent, largely reversible on dose reduction or stopping. Benefits consultants also market the same effect as 'steadiness'.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA requested anhedonia measures in postmarketing studies for retatrutide and in the AUD trials. No label language.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: With ~24M adults now off-drug, regain is a lived experience for millions. Real-world data converge on regain of roughly half to two-thirds of lost weight within 12–18 months, less with structured maintenance.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it drives the chronic-therapy framing and payer reluctance alike.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Further observational reports, especially in older adults and high-dose retatrutide users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Medicare model includes nutrition counselling; no label change.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents and now 6–11-year-olds who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of rigorous follow-up now exists. No data on decades-long use. With ~30% of ever-users cycling, weight-cycling effects on lean mass and metabolism are the most-asked unanswered question.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric 6–11 approval carries a 10-year growth, puberty and bone postmarketing registry requirement. Long-term commitments attached to retatrutide.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Compounding largely ended after the 503B exclusion. Harms have shifted to imported and counterfeit pens, with FDA reporting ~400 adverse-event reports tied to imported product in 2027–28.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised (Nov 2026); CBP seizures of commercial-volume shipments; personal-use import tolerated, not legalised.

safety_ledger.effect: Dysesthesia (skin sensitivity, abnormal sensation) with triple agonism
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seen in retatrutide phase 3 at higher doses. Mostly mild and transient; adds to discontinuation.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume pressure eased as US use halved and stoppers regained. Snack and confectionery volumes recovered about a third of the 2024–26 loss. Companies are quietly trimming 'GLP-1-friendly' SKU ranges while keeping protein callouts and smaller packs, which proved profitable regardless. Analysts cut the 2030 revenue-loss estimates roughly in half.

alcohol.state: Still declining. GLP-1 adoption has receded as an explanation, and Gen Z abstention plus off-label alcohol-reduction prescribing through employee assistance programmes keep pressure on heavy-drinker volumes. Spirits makers cut US guidance again in 2027. Non-alcoholic lines grow, but not enough to offset.

restaurants.state: Traffic stable. Smaller-plate menus stay because they carry better margins. Chains report a partial return of shared appetisers and dessert attach rates in 2028.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists stabilise as regain brings customers back and the body-politics revival lends the category cultural cover. Torrid posts its first flat year since 2024. Mainstream retailers carry wider size runs because customers move between sizes.

fitness.state: 'GLP-1 companion' programmes shrink with the user base. Strength training, sold for muscle preservation, became a habit and outlasted the drugs. Off-drug maintenance programmes, framed as keeping the weight off, are the new growth product.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage fell to 41%. Plans cover diabetes, CVD, sleep apnea and HFpEF codes and exclude obesity alone. A minority of large self-insured employers add adherence-linked premium credits for members with covered metabolic conditions. Pharmacy trend moderated to ~8%.

pharma.state: US volume is down and net price is lower. Lilly's revenue holds on tirzepatide, the orals, retatrutide and its national-champion federal contract. Novo has restructured: cuts of ~9,000 roles, more US fill-finish to avoid tariffs, and growth only outside the US against generics. Global incretin revenue grows more slowly than the 2026 forecasts, now ~$95B in 2028.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A thin body no longer reads clearly as 'on it'. A body that is regaining reads as 'came off', and with ~24M off-drug adults that is now a recognisable look and a source of quiet shame or open defiance. The newest signal is retatrutide-level loss, a near-surgical result that reads as money.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The two tiers have hardened. Salaried workers whose diabetes or cardiac codes are covered, and cash payers at $199–299/month, stay on. Middle-income workers who lost employer weight coverage make up most of the off-drug population. The poorest, through Medicaid and CMAP, now have better access than the middle in some states. Thinness is stratifying around the middle class.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Snacking and second helpings came back in households that stopped. 'Food noise' is now also used for its return. Some evangelical congregations in Dallas–Fort Worth have revived communal fasting as a deliberately drug-free discipline. Potluck culture is a favourite image of the backlash.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles in big cities carry on/off tags. 'Off and staying off' functions as a values signal among under-35 women. In a 2027 survey, ~1 in 6 users reported lower desire. Couples where one partner lost coverage and the other did not are a common subject in advice columns.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: There is a counter-movement. A fat-liberation revival centred in Oakland and Portland, a MAHA-adjacent 'real food, real appetite' current, and church-based 'hunger is holy' framings disagree on almost everything but share one claim: appetite is part of the self, not a symptom. On the other side, appetite as a treatable signal remains medical orthodoxy.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. ~7% of users show a clinically meaningful anhedonia increase vs ~3% background (2027 cohort). Milder 'evenness' is reported far more widely and is not measured. Among the ~5.5M commercially covered users, adherence is now partly paid for through premium credits.
interior_life.framing: Contested. Clinicians call it a side effect. Benefits consultants call it a feature ('the steadiness dividend'). The backlash calls it character theft. Addiction medicine calls it treatment.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Some large self-insured employers in logistics, hospital systems and call centres offer $30–60/month premium credits to members with covered metabolic conditions who keep ≥80% of days covered, verified by PBM refill data. A large PBM's 2027 analysis linked adherence to ~9% fewer absence days and lower turnover; confounding is unaddressed. Supervisors describe adherent staff as 'even' and 'low-drama'. In sales, creative and trading jobs, workers take dose holidays before pitches. Keeping a job with good benefits and staying on the drug now go together, and staying on is partly what keeps the benefits.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: A 'flat era' discourse runs through music and comedy criticism. Austin and Brooklyn comedy scenes trade on-drug and off-drug bits. Sour, spicy and loud flavours stay popular with users. Backlash art celebrates appetite, with feasting imagery and the return of the big plate.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Lower desire is reported by a minority, reversible on dose reduction. Couples negotiate dosing around anniversaries and conception attempts. Couples therapists add 'medication asymmetry' as an intake question.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: An odd coalition, fat-liberation activists, MAHA-aligned parents and libertarian legislators, opposes adherence-linked employer incentives. Illinois and Montana passed medication-privacy-in-employment laws in 2028 barring premium conditioning on refill data. No evidence that blunting affects turnout or partisanship, though op-eds speculate.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-speed on approvals: retatrutide in 13 months, pediatric 6–11 in Oct 2027. Tougher on safety signals: the NAION class warning, and anhedonia measures demanded in postmarketing studies. HHS leadership's 'food first' rhetoric sits uneasily beside White House pricing deals and Lilly procurement.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy: HRSA CMAP provides free Foundayo to up to 1.0M low-income adults (~0.9M enrolled). It is funded from Section 232 tariff receipts at a $100/month contract price, ~$1.1B/yr spent against a $1.2B allocation. Medicare model at $245/$50 copay. No mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: CMAP requires quarterly clinic check-ins and pharmacy refill records. Medicare and commercial plans use BMI and comorbidity prior authorisation. Private employers condition premium credits on PBM-verified adherence, now restricted in Illinois and Montana. No federal rule on employer use of refill data.
state.workforce_or_military: Military accession still disqualifies current GLP-1 users, with waivers debated. TRICARE limits weight-loss coverage. Hiring is not affected by law, but the employer adherence credits in logistics and healthcare are a de facto workforce policy.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 (Apr 2027) put 100% tariffs on imported branded peptide drugs and APIs from firms without US production; onshored output is exempt. Lilly, with US API and fill plants, is the de facto national champion and sole CMAP supplier. Novo moved more fill-finish to North Carolina. China imposed export licensing on peptide intermediates. India's generics flow freely to ~160 countries but not legally to the US. The US-vs-world price gap remains a campaign issue.

events.event: Commerce imposes 100% Section 232 tariffs on imported branded peptide drugs and APIs from manufacturers without US production; Lilly wins sole-source federal supply contract; China responds with export licensing on peptide intermediates
FDA adds class-wide optic-nerve (NAION) warning to all GLP-1-pathway drugs after Sentinel analysis finds roughly doubled risk; new prescriptions fall ~20% in the following quarter
FDA approves Wegovy for children 6–11 with obesity; Medicaid EPSDT coverage follows; 'Let Kids Be Hungry' rallies draw a fat-liberation, church and MAHA-parent crowd in Dallas and Sacramento

HRSA launches Community Metabolic Access Program: free oral Foundayo for up to 1M low-income adults at health centres, funded from tariff receipts; Medicare Bridge pilot succeeded by a narrower CMMI model at $245/$50
FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide, first triple agonist, ~28–30% weight loss, priced at $299/month self-pay; dysesthesia labelled

Employer weight-management coverage falls to 41%; several large self-insured logistics and hospital employers add premium credits for refill-verified adherence among members with covered metabolic conditions; Illinois and Montana bar the practice

open_tensions: The middle has lost the most. Employers dropped weight coverage while the poorest gained free orals and the rich buy retatrutide, and about 24M adults are off-drug and regaining with no payer interested in them.
Employers are paying people to stay on a drug whose reward-blunting effect is suspected and partly marketed as a workplace virtue. States are starting to ban the practice and no federal rule exists.

Tariff money funds a subsidy sole-sourced to a national champion while $10 generics run legally in 160 countries. The arrangement depends on tariffs, on Lilly's goodwill and on a 2031–32 patent cliff.
Children 6–11 are starting a lifelong therapy while 30% of adult ever-users cycle on and off, and there are no data on what decades of cycling do to growing bodies.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; semaglutide exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
Medicare pays ~$245/month for covered obesity treatment with a ~$50 beneficiary copay.
Oral GLP-1 starting doses are still sold at $149 through the TrumpRx cash channel.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 and almost nobody pays it.
The suicidal-ideation warning stays off GLP-1 labels; the effect remains classed as debunked.

prose.headline: Half of America Quit the Shot. The Half That Stayed Has Good Benefits and an Even Temper.
prose.world_in_600_words:
Two years ago one American adult in nine was on a GLP-1 drug for weight. Now it is about one in seventeen, and the change came mostly from people stopping, not from a decision anyone announced. Roughly forty million adults have tried these drugs. About fifteen million are on one now, and twenty-four million are not, many of them partway through regaining. In the last two years almost nobody started for the first time.

Cost explains most of it. Employers kept dropping weight-loss coverage, and by mid-2028 only four in ten cover obesity at all. The rest cover the same molecules for diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea and heart failure, so whether you are covered depends on your diagnosis code. Prices did fall, but slowly: $199 to $299 a month at the cash window, $149 for starter pills, and Wegovy's $1,349 list price untouched. For a warehouse worker who lost coverage in 2027, $249 a month was the gym membership, the car payment and part of the grocery bill combined, so he stopped.

The September 2027 eye warning hurt in a different way. A doubled risk of optic-nerve damage is still very rare in absolute terms, but it is now printed on every pen in the class, and people with doubts had a reason to act on them. Prescriptions fell for a quarter and did not fully recover.

At the bottom of the income scale the picture is reversed. A new federal programme gives away Lilly's daily pill at community health centres, and tariffs pay for it. The Section 232 duties that pushed Novo to move more filling to North Carolina and made Lilly the government's preferred supplier now buy free Foundayo for about nine hundred thousand low-income adults. India sells generic semaglutide for the price of a sandwich and ships it to a hundred and sixty countries. The US is not one of them, and border towns know it.

At the top, Lilly's new triple agonist takes off nearly a third of body weight, close to what surgery achieves, for $299 a month that insurers will not pay. The children's approval in October 2027 put Wegovy in reach of nine-year-olds. Because Medicaid must cover what is medically necessary for children, poor children got access faster than middle-class ones.

Inside workplaces, something quieter is happening. A handful of big self-insured employers in logistics and hospital systems give premium credits to workers with covered metabolic conditions who refill on time, checked against pharmacy records. A pharmacy-benefits analysis said adherent staff miss fewer days. Benefits consultants call this the steadiness dividend. Supervisors talk about 'low-drama' teams. The flattening that patients described in 2026 has a number now, about seven in a hundred users against three in a hundred non-users, and for some employers it has a dollar value. Illinois and Montana banned the credits this year with votes from both left and right.

The backlash is loud and mixed. Fat-liberation organisers in Oakland, megachurch fasting groups outside Dallas and 'real food' parents who distrust the pharmaceutical industry stood together at Sacramento's children's-drug rally without agreeing on much else. Plus-size retail had its first flat year since 2024. Snack volumes came partway back. The drinks industry did not recover, partly because addiction clinics and employee assistance programmes prescribe the drugs off-label to cut drinking.

The country is not thinner or fatter than it was. People in the middle went through a large loss, a partial regain and a lapse in coverage, while those with good benefits or plenty of cash stayed on, and those with little income got the drug free.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Kowalski, fifty-two, wakes at 4:40 in Grove City, Ohio, and injects his Mounjaro into the soft part of his stomach before coffee. It's covered because of his A1C, not his weight. The copay is forty dollars. The app on his phone shows a green checkmark: ninety-one percent days covered, so another fifty-dollar premium credit next month.

At the distribution centre he runs second shift's handoff. A picker yells about a mis-slotted pallet and Ray just nods and fixes it. His manager calls that being steady. Ray thinks it's more like the volume knob on everything got turned down.

Lunch is half a turkey wrap. The other half goes back in the cooler.

Lori texts at two: church tonight, potluck, you coming? She stopped Zepbound last March, when the company dropped weight coverage and the cash price would have been two-forty-nine. She's put back about thirty pounds. She says she feels like herself. At Calvary they call it reclaiming hunger. She brings her lasagna, the real one.

He goes. A woman by the coffee urn asks if he's still on it, kindly, the way you'd ask about a divorce. He says it's for sugar. That's true.

Lori laughs at something across the room, loud. He used to laugh like that during Browns games. Last Sunday he watched the fourth quarter and felt nothing in particular and went to bed.

At home she leaves a slice of cake on the counter for him. He looks at it for a while, puts plastic wrap over it and slides it into the fridge.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Illinois and Montana passed medication-privacy-in-employment laws in 2028 barring premium conditioning on refill data.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: Montana's legislature does not meet in regular session in even years, and no chain explains how two states legislate within months of employers first adding adherence credits (the June 2028 event). The law-passing is asserted for narrative symmetry.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Direct subsidy: HRSA CMAP provides free Foundayo to up to 1.0M low-income adults (~0.9M enrolled).
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: a programme launched in Jan 2028 at community health centres is shown 90% enrolled within the window. Most of these adults would be first-time starters, which sits uneasily with the claim that first-time starts were only ~0.4 pp (~1.06M) across 2027–28, a total that must also cover retatrutide, children and others.

least_plausible_claims.quote: commercial ~5.5M (mostly under diabetes or CVD codes)
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the population note says the series is the Gallup weight-loss measure and that incretin use coded purely to type 2 diabetes sits mostly outside it. Yet over a third of the 15.6M counted users are described as covered under diabetes or CVD codes, so the payer mix and the series definition do not cleanly reconcile.

rationale.badness: A middle class priced off the drug (about 24M off and regaining) sits beside employer adherence credits tied to PBM refill data (the `interior_life` and `state.conditioning` fields). Anhedonia in ~7% of users is measured but unlabelled, and 6–11-year-olds start lifelong therapy. Offsets are real: free CMAP orals for the poorest, a measured and named NAION warning, and state pushback. This is a recognisably harder society with new losers (the middle, children, workers with conditioned benefits), not a refuse-to-live-in one.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised and traceable to events and fields, including adoption at 5.9, the Sep 2027 NAION class label, pediatric 6–11 approval, retatrutide approved 13 months after its Feb 2027 filing (inside the ≥12-month rule), Section 232 tariffs, CMAP and the employer credits. mechanism: the main chains are shown (coverage loss, NAION label, regain and backlash), but the Montana 2028 law, the rapid CMAP enrolment and employee assistance programmes 'prescribing' are asserted without a chain (claims 1–2). magnitude: on-drug 5.9, ever-used 15, income thirds (average 5.9) and age bands (about 5.9) are all inside the envelope, and the payer mix sums to 15.6M. The Medicare, Medicaid and CMAP spend arithmetic checks out, and no US generic appears. Minor flaws remain: diabetes-coded users counted in a weight-loss series, and the tight fit between 0.4 pp first-time starts and the CMAP and retatrutide uptake (claims 2–3).
rationale.generativity: The world has strong implied scenes: potluck at Calvary, the green checkmark and premium credit, dose holidays before pitches, on/off dating tags, and the Sacramento rally. The Ray and Lori vignette shows rather than explains (the cake under plastic wrap, the flat Browns Sunday), and the open tensions give many threads. Characters and institutions are specific and varied across class, region and age.

least_plausible_claims.quote: First-time starts fell to roughly 0.4 pp of adults over 2027–28, inside the survey margin, so ever-used still reads 15%.
least_plausible_claims.why: The same world has ~0.9M adults enrolled in the new CMAP, a Medicare model with ~2.1M users, and ~220k children. Many of these must be first-time starts, and they alone exceed 0.4 pp (~1.06M adults). This fails magnitude and reconciliation, and it makes the prose line 'almost nobody started for the first time' contradict the access fields.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Illinois and Montana passed medication-privacy-in-employment laws in 2028 barring premium conditioning on refill data.
least_plausible_claims.why: The employer credits are described as a new practice by a handful of firms, and the bans are dated the same month (2028-06) as their adoption. Montana's legislature meets only in odd-numbered years, so a 2028 law is implausible without a special session. This fails mechanism on timing.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Some employee assistance programmes and addiction clinics prescribe off-label
least_plausible_claims.why: EAPs are counselling and referral services and do not prescribe drugs. Treating them as a prescribing channel that moves heavy-drinker volumes, as the alcohol section does, is an asserted mechanism. No AUD approval or phase 3 result exists to support it, so it fails mechanism.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder society with new losers. About 24M adults are off-drug and regaining, and middle-income workers have lost employer coverage. PBM-verified adherence credits tie benefits to staying on a drug with suspected reward blunting (interior_life, state/conditioning). Children aged 6–11 start lifelong therapy with a stratified access pattern. Mitigants: the poorest gain free orals via CMAP, the harms are measured (the anhedonia cohort, the NAION label), and states are already pushing back, so epistemic and flourishing scores stay moderate.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised and traceable to events or fields. Adoption is 5.9%, employer coverage is 41%, the NAION label is dated Sep 2027, retatrutide is filed Feb 2027 and approved Mar 2028 under the 12-month rule, and the tariffs, CMAP subsidy, backlash, pediatric 6–11 approval and employer adherence credits all appear. mechanism: Most chains are shown (coverage loss and the NAION warning driving exits, tariffs funding CMAP). Claims 1–3 weaken it: the 'almost nobody started' claim contradicts CMAP and the Medicare model, the Montana ban lacks a plausible legislative path, and EAP prescribing is a convenient assertion. magnitude: Population figures sit inside the envelope (5.9% on drug, 15% ever). The age-band and income-third averages, the payer mix (sums to 15.6M) and the spend arithmetic ($6.2B, $3.8B, $1.1B) all check out. The first-time-starts figure of ~1M conflicts with the new public programmes, which is a minor reconciliation gap (claim 1).
rationale.generativity: The world is rich in implied characters and scenes: a warehouse worker on refill credits, the Calvary potluck with 'reclaiming hunger', dose holidays before pitches, couples negotiating dosing, on/off dating tags, and the Sacramento rally. The day-in-the-life shows rather than explains, for example the cake under plastic wrap and the 'volume knob' line. Ray's lived texture is strong, with the credit app, the half wrap and the 'it's for sugar' answer.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Illinois and Montana passed medication-privacy-in-employment laws in 2028 barring premium conditioning on refill data.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: Montana's legislature meets only in odd years, so a 2028 enactment has no shown route. Neither does a bill drafted and passed in states within months of the first employer credits, and no special session is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: First-time starts fell to roughly 0.4 pp of adults over 2027–28, inside the survey margin, so ever-used still reads 15%.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: CMAP's 0.9M free slots alone are about 0.34 pp of adults and are likely mostly new starters. Add the new Medicare model, the pediatric approval and retatrutide, and near-zero first-time use is hard to believe. Holding ever-used at exactly 15 looks reverse-engineered to fit the envelope ceiling.

least_plausible_claims.quote: commercial ~5.5M (mostly under diabetes or CVD codes)
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and reconciliation: the population note says the series follows the Gallup weight-loss measure and that T2D-coded use sits mostly outside it. Yet most commercial 'weight-loss users' are diabetes- or CVD-coded, and Ray, on Mounjaro for his A1C, is counted. The counting rule is inconsistent.

rationale.badness: The world is recognisably harder, with new losers. About 24M adults are off-drug and regaining, and middle-income people lost coverage. Employers pay premium credits for PBM-verified adherence (interior_life, state/conditioning), and children 6–11 start lifelong therapy. Offsetting this, the poor get free orals, the NAION risk is measured, and the anhedonia effect is quantified and largely reversible, so the harms are visible and contested rather than hidden.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers appear and are traceable. Adoption is 11→5.9, the NAION class label is Sep 2027, retatrutide is approved 13 months after filing, the pediatric 6–11 approval is Oct 2027, and the Section 232 tariffs, the CMAP subsidy, employer-encouraged adherence credits, employer retreat and the backlash are all present. mechanism: Most changes have chains (coverage loss, the label and cost driving stoppage, tariffs funding CMAP), but near-zero first-time starts despite CMAP, Medicare and pediatric access is asserted (claim 2). The diabetes-coded users counted in a weight-loss series is inconsistent (claim 3), and the Montana law in 2028 is unexplained (claim 1). magnitude: Current use 5.9, ever-used 15 (at the envelope ceiling), the income thirds (average 5.9) and the age bands (≈5.9) all fit the envelope. The ever/current/cycling arithmetic and the payer-mix and spend figures reconcile (15.6M, $6.2B, $3.8B, $1.1B). The ever-used ceiling and the 0.4 pp starts are strained.
rationale.generativity: The prose has strong scenes: Ray's premium-credit app, the potluck at Calvary, the untouched cake. The world supplies many implied characters (the warehouse worker, Lori, the supervisors, the clinic and CMAP enrollees) and concrete settings (Dallas, Oakland, Sacramento). It shows more than it explains, though some of the prose is summary.

least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: Montana's legislature does not meet in regular session in even years, and no chain explains how two states legislate within months of employers first adding adherence credits (the June 2028 event). The law-passing is asserted for narrative symmetry.

Most of these adults would be first-time starters, which sits uneasily with the claim that first-time starts were only ~0.4 pp (~1.06M) across 2027–28, a total that must also cover retatrutide, children and others.

least_plausible_claims.quote: commercial ~5.5M (mostly under diabetes or CVD codes)
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the population note says the series is the Gallup weight-loss measure and that incretin use coded purely to type 2 diabetes sits mostly outside it. Yet over a third of the 15.6M counted users are described as covered under diabetes or CVD codes, so the payer mix and the series definition do not cleanly reconcile.

rationale.badness: A middle class priced off the drug (about 24M off and regaining) sits beside employer adherence credits tied to PBM refill data (the `interior_life` and `state.conditioning` fields). Anhedonia in ~7% of users is measured but unlabelled, and 6–11-year-olds start lifelong therapy. Offsets are real: free CMAP orals for the poorest, a measured and named NAION warning, and state pushback. This is a recognisably harder society with new losers (the middle, children, workers with conditioned benefits), not a refuse-to-live-in one.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised and traceable to events and fields, including adoption at 5.9, the Sep 2027 NAION class label, pediatric 6–11 approval, retatrutide approved 13 months after its Feb 2027 filing (inside the ≥12-month rule), Section 232 tariffs, CMAP and the employer credits. mechanism: the main chains are shown (coverage loss, NAION label, regain and backlash), but the Montana 2028 law, the rapid CMAP enrolment and employee assistance programmes 'prescribing' are asserted without a chain (claims 1–2). magnitude: on-drug 5.9, ever-used 15, income thirds (average 5.9) and age bands (about 5.9) are all inside the envelope, and the payer mix sums to 15.6M. The Medicare, Medicaid and CMAP spend arithmetic checks out, and no US generic appears. Minor flaws remain: diabetes-coded users counted in a weight-loss series, and the tight fit between 0.4 pp first-time starts and the CMAP and retatrutide uptake (claims 2–3).
rationale.generativity: The world has strong implied scenes: potluck at Calvary, the green checkmark and premium credit, dose holidays before pitches, on/off dating tags, and the Sacramento rally. The Ray and Lori vignette shows rather than explains (the cake under plastic wrap, the flat Browns Sunday), and the open tensions give many threads. Characters and institutions are specific and varied across class, region and age.
